niche: polymer distributor's bulk silo programme: the one-grade tonnage nominated for a plan year across customer moulding plants
answer: We nominate 9,669 tonnes of HM-233 on the bulk silo programme for plan year 2028.
stakeholder_role: demand planning lead at a polymer distributor

spine.entity: one despatch line of a part's resin to a customer plant
spine.grain: plant x part x despatch line

world.geography: United States, Midwest (Indiana, Ohio, Michigan, Wisconsin, Illinois)

driver: Eligibility for a fixed commitment turns on whether each site's receiving capacity can take one full delivery on top of the stock the site must already be holding when a delivery can land, which is the draw across the supplier's call-off-to-delivery window at the site's own peak on its period profile, so the largest requirements at the smallest receivers drop out, and the residence limit shortens by the same window because the delivery waits behind that stock.
driver_concrete: A plant joins the HM-233 silo programme only if its silo can take a 24-tonne T24 discharge on top of the two weeks of draw it must be holding when a load is called off (terms 2.1 has a load called off when the silo, counting loads already called off, is down to the plant's next two weeks on the plan, and the producer can discharge it that day), tested at the plant's busiest two weeks on the period plan, and only if the load then clears inside the six weeks of silo life it has left behind that cover: 9 plants and 9,669 tonnes, against the 15 plants and 15,915 tonnes the empty-silo eight-week reading files.
stump: A competent solver builds the qualified requirement, applies 2.4's three limbs with the eight-week rolling minimum on the period plan, tests the silo limb as a static capacity of at least 24 t, and files the eight-week figure; it never asks what the silo is already holding when a load lands, so it keeps the big plants whose silos cannot take a load on top of two weeks' draw and the seasonal plants whose load waits behind that cover past its eight weeks.

differentiation.task94: the v3 re-root moves the decisive test from the trough of the period profile (the eight-week minimum, now a solved middle rung) to its peak against the receiving silo, through the cover a continuous supply forces the plant to hold across the call-off window
differentiation.task37: task37 grades completions under a places cap and a fill floor on a cohort schedule; task94 grades a supply tonnage whose plants drop out because a silo cannot hold a load on top of the cover a call-off window forces
differentiation.task69: task69's marketplace builds turn on reconstructing assignment and allocation; task94 turns on a receiving capacity tested at the peak of a forward period profile through a lead-time cover
differentiation.task87: task87 resolves the unit a funding cap counts through a group ruling; task94 tests each plant's silo against a load plus the peak draw across a call-off window
differentiation.task28: different world and move: task94's constraint is a receiving capacity against peak window draw on a forward plan
differentiation.task32: different world and move: task94's constraint is a receiving capacity against peak window draw on a forward plan
differentiation.task51: task51 recovers a register's own reclassification rule; task94 has no recovered rule, the constraint is filed facts composed into a peak test
differentiation.task53: task53 splits addressable volume on a break in one column; task94's drawable set is a two-sided band in silo against peak and trough of the profile, which no column cut reproduces

lineage.fate: solved on the portal: both top responses filed the ground truth (reported 2026-09-14); re-rooted the same day
lineage.driver: A committed volume is the part of a correctly built requirement drawable where a full delivery increment fits the receiving unit and the unit's average rate turns it over inside a shelf-life limit, with the requirement built over every item approved for the grade rather than the grade's own book.

lineage.driver: Eligibility for a fixed commitment is tested on each site's minimum draw over a rolling window of its period profile rather than on its average rate, and because profile shape is independent of size the committed set is not the top of any reported column and the total falls well below the average-rate reading.
